title: Write-guard containment allowlist for harness memory and scratchpad roots
action: Per guard-hardening E1 (CONTEXT.md) and the plan Constraints. Implement the containment allowlist: after the existing canonical resolution of a write target (Edit/Write/MultiEdit AND extracted Bash targets), if the RESOLVED path is under <home>/.claude/projects/ or <system-temp>/claude/, the outside-root containment deny does not fire. Scope strictly: the exemption bypasses ONLY the containment deny - reservation/hold checks, gate-boundary checks, direct-edit denies and secret checks still run where applicable (in practice out-of-root paths do not hit repo-relative checks, but the code order must make that true by construction, not by accident). Fail-closed: if home or temp cannot be resolved, the allowlist contributes nothing and the deny stands. Resolve home and temp the way existing code in this crate does (search for existing home_dir/temp usage - onboard/source.rs has home_dir); on Windows honor the actual system temp (std::env::temp_dir). Find the containment failure emission (write_guard/main.rs around lines 177-228, the could-not-be-canonically-contained message) and thread the allowlist there for both the ordinary-checkout and granted-worktree shapes. Add unit tests beside the existing write_guard test style covering: (1) write to <home>/.claude/projects/x/memory/f.md allowed, (2) write to <temp>/claude/s/scratchpad/f.txt allowed, (3) write to a sibling worktree path still denied, (4) a traversal spelling (repo/../../.claude/projects/...) judged by resolved location - allowed only if resolved into an allowlist root, (5) unrelated out-of-root absolute path still denied, (6) unresolvable home/temp leaves deny intact (simulate via the code's seam, e.g. injectable roots - prefer parameterizing the check function with the roots so tests need no env mutation). Existing tests must pass unmodified; if one must change, STOP and report. Run the write-guard-focused tests plus the full suite (commands.test) and quote both summaries.

truths: resolved-path allowlist covers home .claude/projects and system-temp claude roots only
containment deny unchanged for every other out-of-root target
fail-closed on unresolvable home/temp, proven by a test

title: Extend the CLI-owned direct-edit deny set to cells, lanes and onboarding
action: Per guard-hardening E2 (CONTEXT.md) and the plan Constraints. Extend direct_edit_verb (write_guard/guards.rs:41-52) so hand-edits via Edit/Write/MultiEdit/Bash-mutation are denied for: .bee/cells/*.json, .bee/lanes/*.json, .bee/onboarding.json - matching style consistent with the existing five enumerated entries (the existing set matches exact relative paths; for cells/lanes use a prefix+extension match in the same function, keep it readable). EXPLICITLY preserved as writable: .bee/config.json and .bee/decisions.jsonl (sanctioned agent surfaces) - do not touch scratch_shape_deny allowances. Check the deny message names the owning CLI verb (cells add/finish, state lanes/start-feature --as-lane, onboard) so the agent hitting it knows the sanctioned path. Add regression tests asserting: deny on a .bee/cells/x.json edit, deny on .bee/lanes/x.json, deny on .bee/onboarding.json, ALLOW preserved on .bee/config.json and .bee/decisions.jsonl. Existing tests must pass unmodified; a required change to one is STOP-and-report. Run the full suite (commands.test) and quote the summary.

truths: cells, lanes and onboarding.json hand-edits denied with a message naming the owning verb
config.json and decisions.jsonl remain writable, proven by tests

title: grep/find permissions.deny plus the markdown-only-by-necessity record
action: Per guard-hardening E3+E5 (CONTEXT.md) and the plan Constraints. (1) E3: edit .claude/settings.json - inside the existing permissions object (currently {"defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"}) add "deny": ["Bash(grep:*)", "Bash(find:*)"]. Touch nothing else in the file; valid JSON; note in your report that onboarding preserves this key (onboard/tests.rs test repo_hooks_wires_both_projections_and_preserves_foreign_entries). (2) E5: sync doctrine - in unenforced-obedience.md add (in its own format, citing guard-hardening E5) the record of which boundary rules stay markdown-only by necessity and why: gate self-approval (actor identity unknowable to the CLI), independent-review-never-automatic, claim-only-via-claim-next; note build-on-red is CLI-enforced at bee cells finish and where the newly-enforced rules moved (E1/E2/E3). In prompt-writing-standard.md's deterministic-backstop section add one sentence pointing at the deny entries as the live example (cite guard-hardening E3). Respect both files' formats; citations must resolve (pointer_integrity). (3) Author docs/history/learnings/20260803-guard-hardening.md: what was enforced vs left markdown-only and why, the E1 narrowing story (user asked to drop containment; allowlist met the need), and the settings-preservation proof point. (4) Run the full suite (commands.test) and quote the summary; also run the knowledge index regen check (bee knowledge index --check; regenerate via bee knowledge index if the two parent indexes go stale from your edits).
